title: Creating Python Date Objects
learningObjectives: Explain constructing and parsing calendar dates and its role in Python applications.
Choose appropriate datetime classes and methods for constructing and parsing calendar dates.
Predict the output of representative PY17.2 operations.
Identify invalid values, formatting ambiguity or timezone risks related to constructing and parsing calendar dates.
Apply constructing and parsing calendar dates in a small, deterministic Python program.

understand.concept: A date object represents a valid calendar day using year, month and day fields. Construct it with `date(year, month, day)` or parse an ISO date string with `date.fromisoformat()`. Invalid calendar values raise ValueError instead of silently rolling into another month.
understand.whyItMatters: Validated date objects make comparisons and date calculations safer than comparing unvalidated strings.
understand.analogy: Date-time values are like entries on a calendar plus the hands on a clock; a duration measures the distance between two entries.
understand.analogyLimit: Real calendars include leap years, time zones and daylight-saving transitions that a simple wall calendar analogy does not fully model.
understand.summary: Creating Python Date Objects teaches reliable representation and manipulation of Python date-time values.

explain.narrative:
## Construct a date
Use `datetime.date(year, month, day)`. The constructor validates the calendar fields, including month length and leap years.

## Parse ISO dates
`date.fromisoformat('YYYY-MM-DD')` converts a standard ISO date string to a date object. Validate external input and handle ValueError when the string is malformed or represents an impossible date.

## Read and replace fields
The `year`, `month` and `day` attributes expose the components. `replace()` returns a new date with selected fields changed; date objects are immutable.

## Keep data types consistent
Compare date objects with date objects, not with arbitrary strings. Convert input at the boundary, then perform date logic using the date API.

examples.title: Construct a date explicitly
examples.code:
from datetime import date
launch = date(2025, 4, 12)
print(launch.year, launch.month, launch.day)
examples.explanation: The constructor accepts year, month and day as integer arguments.

examples.title: Parse an ISO date string
examples.code:
from datetime import date
value = date.fromisoformat('2024-02-29')
print(value)
print(value.year)

examples.title: Reject an impossible date
examples.explanation: 2025 is not a leap year, so February 29 is invalid.

examples.title: Replace one date field
examples.code:
from datetime import date
original = date(2026, 3, 14)
changed = original.replace(year=2027)
print(original)
print(changed)
examples.explanation: replace returns a new date and leaves the original unchanged.

examples.title: Compare two dates
examples.code:
from datetime import date
first = date(2026, 1, 10)
second = date(2026, 1, 15)
print(first < second)
print((second - first).days)
examples.explanation: Date ordering and subtraction are supported directly.

practise.guidedTask: Create a deterministic program demonstrating constructing and parsing calendar dates. Predict the result first, run the code, then explain the date-time values and operations used.
practise.independentTask: Build a small scheduling or reporting utility using constructing and parsing calendar dates. Include a valid case, a boundary case and an explanation of how invalid or ambiguous input is handled.
hints: Use date, time, datetime or timedelta according to the value you need to represent.
Prefer explicit constructors and ISO-formatted input for predictable examples.
Check calendar boundaries and invalid values instead of assuming every date exists.
Use documented format directives and distinguish formatting from parsing.
Make timezone assumptions explicit whenever a value represents a real-world instant.
practise.challenge: Extend the examples into a small appointment scheduler that validates dates, calculates durations and formats output without relying on the machine's current clock.
validationCriteria: The program uses the appropriate datetime class or method.
The expected output matches the actual result.
Invalid or boundary values are handled deliberately.
Timezone assumptions are explicit where relevant.

questions.prompt: Which constructor creates a date object?
questions.explanation: date takes year, month and day.
fromisoformat parses supported ISO date text.

questions.prompt: What happens when an impossible date is constructed?
options: The date silently moves to the next month

questions.prompt: What does replace() return on a date object?
questions.answer: A new date with selected fields changed
options: A new date with selected fields changed
questions.explanation: Date objects are immutable; replace creates a new value.

questions.prompt: Can two date objects be compared with < ?
options: No, only strings can be compared
Only if they are the same day
